newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts up ahead of U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts up ahead of U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Latin Brady bond prices rose with U.S. Treasuries but spreads ended mixed, while Russia and Bulgaria papers staged a mild technical recovery from Wednesday's drop, emerging market debt traders said.
Mexico's Bradies and eurobonds climbed on the coattail of its successful 10-year note offer. Mexico UMS-26 MXUMS=RR rose 1-1/8 to 106-1/8. Mexico Pars, Discounts and Aztec all made gains.
"The new paper traded well after-market," said a trader at a U.S. investment house. The 10-year global was priced to yield 335 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Among other major Latin Bradies, spreads on Venezuela papers were tighter but Brazil widened a bit. Prices on Argentina Bradies firmed but lagging U.S. Treasuries, the trader said.
Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 7/8 to 62-3/8, Brazil C BR8D14=RR added 3/8 to 74-3/8 and Venezuela DCBs VZFLL07=RR was up 1/2 at 88-1/4.
"People are cautious before the jobs number," he said. The December non-farm payrolls report will be released at 0830 EST on Friday.
Russia Vnesh loans crawled from Wednesday's selloff as President Boris Yeltsin's condition appeared to be stable after being admitted to the hospital.
"People are still worried about Yeltsin," said the trader. "But the selloff (on Wednesday) was overdone."
Russia dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR rose 3/4 to 78-1/2.
Bulgaria papers had a bid tone, but buying interest was light. "The political and economic problems there don't change day-to-day," he said.
